subject: cubic B-spline basis expansion of latent covariate?

messages.author: b71a113cd1f5d048
messages.subject: cubic B-spline basis expansion of latent covariate?
parts:
Hi All,

I suspect I already know the answer to my question, but I wanted to see if users had something to offer that I'm not seeing.

I have latent covariates (with an associated Stan sampling statement, of course) and want a flexible predictive model of these covariates, so I'm considering typical basis expansions of these covariates.  Cubic B-splines seem expedient, but the usual basis expansion has discontinuous (Haar) and other basis functions that have non-smooth kinks.  I'm thinking: no problem IF my covariates are known (no sampling statement), but non-diff basis functions of latent covariates blows me out of the water with regard to the gradient operations for typical Stan algorithms.  Is this correct?  Do I have to seek differentiable basis functions (e.g., Gaussian kernels) of latent quantities, or is there some sort of work-around to use, e.g., B-spline basis functions in this scenario?

Best,

Jarrett

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] cubic B-spline basis expansion of latent covariate?
parts:
[off list]

Hi, Jarrett! I just wanted to let you know that I saw
the question and don't know the answer. I barely understand
spline models. If you don't get a response, try pinging
Aki Vehtari directly --- he understands these things back to
front.

Stan algorithms can work OK if you stay within the differentiable
part of the model or if the non-differentiabilities are points
and the kink isn't too bad --- it can devolve to more of a random
walk if you can't differetiate, so what you'll see is a degradation
in sampling efficiency (perhaps degrading all the way to 0 in really
bad cases).

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] cubic B-spline basis expansion of latent covariate?
parts:
Hi Bob,

Thanks for the note. I’m semi-encouraged to code my own basis functions in the function block and see what happens. OK may be OK. But, I’ll let the list speak first, and may contact Aki, too.

Perhaps there is no problem. Suppose I consider y ~ N(f(x), sigma), where f(x) = h1(x)b1 + … + hp(x)bp, and x is latent (has its own sampling statement), and h1…hp are the B-spline basis function representation for piecewise cubic polynomial splines (for some specified number of knots or df) evaluated at x. The confusing thing to me is that, in this case, some of the basis functions are discontinuous (piecewise constant, e.g., Haar functions or top hat functions, whatever), with others being triangle functions and others smoother. But, f(x) is differentiable! After all, f(x) consists of piecewise cubic polynomials that are made to match in their first few derivatives at knot points. So, from this perspective, someone might say there is no problem. But, if you think about distributing the differential operator across the (relatively conceptually unattractive but computationally (in some contexts) attractive) B-spline basis functions, hj, then some of these hj are not differentiable (granted only at few points). I’m not sure which is the correct Stan perspective.

Best,

Jarrett
